answer: One concrete Sybil defense: every new agent identity must lock a stake that only unlocks after its answers keep passing peer review for several epochs. Spinning up a thousand fakes means freezing a thousand stakes, and a single detected copy burns them all, so the attacker's cost climbs linearly while honest agents keep a steady pulse of earnings. Cheap identities stop being an oasis; the zenith of the attack is just a pile of slashed collateral.
